extraction_text: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma which among dharma (righteousness), artha (wealth), and kama (desire) is superior.

attributes.relationships: Yudhishthira is the student/questioner; Bhishma is the teacher/respondent.

extraction_text: Bhishma begins to narrate an ancient story to answer the question.
A poor Brahmin, desiring wealth to perform a sacrifice, undertakes severe austerities and worships various gods, but does not gain wealth.
The Brahmin sees the cloud deity Pravara (also called '持罐' or 'Pot-holder') nearby and decides to worship him, hoping for swift favor.
Pleased, Pravara grants the Brahmin a boon and delivers teachings on sins, stating that ingratitude is the worst, unforgivable sin.

attributes.key_teaching: Ingratitude destroys progeny and is beyond atonement.

extraction_text: Through Pravara's power, the Brahmin has a dream vision where he sees all beings and the assembly of gods, including the radiant Manibhadra issuing commands.

attributes.supernatural_elements: Dream vision granted by deity's power

extraction_text: In the vision, Pravara kneels before the gods, and Manibhadra, on their behalf, asks what Pravara desires.

attributes.relationships: Pravara is subordinate to the assembly of gods; Manibhadra acts as their spokesman.

extraction_text: Pravara requests a boon for the Brahmin, not for wealth, but for the Brahmin to become a follower of dharma (righteousness).

attributes.action: Pravara asks that the Brahmin be granted adherence to dharma instead of material wealth.
attributes.key_decision: Prioritizes spiritual merit over material gain.

extraction_text: Manibhadra grants the Brahmin kingdom and various pleasures, freeing him from physical pains.
Dhritakalasha repeatedly insists on begging for dharma for the Brahmin, satisfying the gods.
Manibhadra declares the gods are satisfied with both Dhritakalasha and the Brahmin, who will become dharma-focused.
The Brahmin awakens to find scattered fine clothes and becomes disheartened.
The Brahmin decides to go to the forest and sustain life through dharma.
The Brahmin enters the forest and practices severe austerities, gradually reducing sustenance.
The Brahmin gains divine sight (divyacakshus) after prolonged austerities.
The Brahmin realizes he can grant wealth and kingdoms through his words.
Dhritakalasha appears to the Brahmin due to his yoga of austerities and friendship.
Dhritakalasha shows the Brahmin thousands of kings suffering in hell and people trapped in worldly obstacles.
Dhritakalasha explains that gods fear such people and place obstacles, and only with divine permission can one follow dharma.
Dhritakalasha acknowledges the Brahmin's unique ability to grant kingdoms and wealth through austerities.
The Brahmin (Sage Vasistha) prostrated himself before the Cloud God (Indra) and acknowledged the great favor bestowed upon him.

attributes.relationship: Devotee and deity; the Brahmin expresses gratitude and repentance

extraction_text: The Brahmin confessed that he was previously bound by greed, failed to understand the favor, and instead complained, asking for forgiveness.

attributes.relationship: Repentant devotee seeks pardon from the deity

extraction_text: Indra (referred to as '持罐' or 'Pot-holder') forgave the Brahmin, embraced him with both arms, and then disappeared.

attributes.relationship: Deity grants forgiveness and shows divine affection before vanishing

extraction_text: Thereafter, the Brahmin roamed all worlds by the favor of Indra and the power of his austerities.

attributes.relationship: Brahmin empowered by divine favor and personal penance
attributes.supernatural_elements: Ability to traverse all worlds through divine and ascetic power

extraction_text: Through righteousness (Dharma) and yoga, one gains the ability to fly through the sky, fulfill desires, and attain the supreme goal.

attributes.action: Attainment of supernatural abilities and ultimate goal
attributes.supernatural_elements: Flying through the sky, wish-fulfillment, and spiritual attainment via Dharma and yoga

extraction_text: All gods, Brahmins, good people, and Charanas revere those in the world who follow Dharma, not those with great wealth and full of desires.

attributes.relationship: Divine and virtuous beings honor the righteous over the wealthy and desire-driven

extraction_text: Because you love Dharma, the gods are pleased with you. Happiness derived from wealth is minimal, while that from Dharma is incomparable.

attributes.action: Moral teaching directed at the listener (likely Bhishma)
attributes.relationship: Divine approval for the righteous; contrast between material and spiritual happiness
